subject: Information Theory
title: Poetry and Constraint
description: A quick win: understand Poetry and Constraint.

hook.text: A sonnet must have 14 lines, iambic pentameter, and a specific rhyme scheme. Constraints make it harder—and richer.

buildup.text: Poetic forms add extra redundancy: rhyme, meter, and structure all constrain word choices beyond normal grammar.

discovery.text: More constraints mean fewer valid completions. Each word carries more information because fewer words could fit.

twist.text: This is why poetry feels dense with meaning. The constraints force the poet to pack more information per word.

climax.text: Information theory explains the paradox: restrictions increase the information value of each surviving choice.

punchline.text: More constraints, more meaning per word. Structure creates depth.

quiz.question: Why does constrained poetry feel dense with meaning?
options: Constraints make each word choice carry more information
